column1: # Pokémon Mystery Dungeon Rescue Team DX 1.0.2 (update v131072): Unity 2018.3.12f1 IL2CPP with FMOD on SDK 7.4.0, NVN; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie. Started from porter's
# provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and checked by hand against the survey; Android testing is in android.tsv.
# patches.py: Unity 2018.3's render command stream (ThreadedStreamBuffer) wakes its reader and writer with a flag and a store-release, then a plain load: the main thread and
# UnityGfxDeviceWorker each slept waiting for the other within seconds of every launch (a black screen); the cuts make those loads ldar.

column1: # the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main sets a heap: a 5 GB block with a large alias region (the layout of the other Unity 2018 games,
# Lonely Mountains: Downhill). No heap check was run (it boots the game on the Mac host): the guessed keys held through the opening and Tiny Woods (footprint about 1.7 GB)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game asks for present interval 2 (Unity's vSyncCount), which display mode ignores, and nothing else holds it at 30 (frame work about 3 ms on an
# Adreno 740). The dungeon steps by the time that really passed: on the Odin 2, holding up for 1 s at 60 fps and then down for 1 s pinned at 30 (DM_FPS_PIN, one run) walked back
# to the same tile, one belly point a step both ways; frame counting would have walked twice as far up. DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=game in env.txt keeps 30 and saves power
